authorization: owner, 2026-10-09: 'create the thumbnail and title options'

rules: Built from the episode's own cold-open cast and set, not invented people or working-model sketches.
Presenter in frame at about one third, on the right, serious rather than smiling; the story plays behind him.
Thumbnail text speaks to the viewer's aspiration in this episode's own terms: the verb of the one-person business. EP007 was HELP HER SELL.
Title promises the viewer will learn to run the business. Not a problem frame.
Mock feed against real comps at desktop, phone and sidebar, plus a shrink test at 168 and 320 px on white and #0f0f0f, before any pick.

cold_open.verbatim_opening: An innkeeper with twenty rooms is closing out a reservation. Good guest. Three nights, tipped housekeeping, asked about the trail behind the property. The kind of person she'd like to see again. So she goes to send a thank you note. And the email on the reservation isn't his.
cold_open.cast: The innkeeper, a woman in an olive cardigan over a cream top, dark hair in a low bun, behind a wooden front desk. The departing guest, a man with a backpack and dark jacket.
cold_open.set: A small country inn front desk: laptop, brass call bell, a glass of yellow daffodils, an open ledger, mail pigeonholes behind, windows onto woods.
cold_open.object: The reservation card showing the relay address k7m2q9x4@guest.booking.com.

titles.text: The One-Person Business That Gets Small Hotels Booking Direct
titles.note: Closest to EP007's accepted shape: names the business and what it does for the client. The verb 'gets ... booking direct' is the service's function, not an outcome promise.

titles.text: The One-Person Business Behind a Hotel's Direct Bookings
titles.note: Shorter, more curiosity than instruction. Reads well truncated on mobile, which cuts around 50 characters.

titles.text: How to Run the One-Person Business That Wins a Hotel's Guests Back
titles.note: Most explicitly a how-to, which is the instruction in the standard. Longest, and 'wins back' is close to EP006's retired WIN THEM BACK.

thumbnail_text.note: The literal verb of the service. Four words is one more than HELP HER SELL and will set smaller.
Three words, same metre as HELP HER SELL. 'Keep' is the innkeeper's aspiration, the returning guest she already knows.
Names the mechanism the episode and Short 03 both turn on. Drops the HELP HER pattern, so it reads as a different family.

recommendation.title: T1
recommendation.why: T1 matches the shape the owner already picked once and keeps the promise on the service's function rather than an outcome. X2 holds the HELP HER metre so the lockup sets at the same weight as EP007's, and 'keep them' is the innkeeper's aspiration in the cold open: the guest she would like to see again. X1 is more literal but sets smaller; X3 is the strongest line on its own and the weakest as a series.

claim_boundaries: 'Help' and 'gets ... booking direct' keep the promise on the practice's function. No claim that the service recovers a given share, saves a given amount, or that any property pays.
No figure on the thumbnail or in the title. No income framing.

Every person in the frame is AI-generated: the innkeeper and guest are the episode's own synthetic footage, the presenter is the avatar. Covered by the upload's altered-or-synthetic-content disclosure, which is a human step at upload.

plan.generator: Higgsfield gpt_image_2_5, the same route EP007 used
plan.rounds: three compositions, one per thumbnail text, then a mock feed and shrink test
plan.cap: under 10 credits for exploration, matching EP007's 7.25
plan.not_included: no 4K upscale until a pick is made; that was a separate 2-credit job on EP007

shrink_test_reading: At 168px, which is the sidebar and small-mobile size, X2 is the only one that still reads as three distinct words. X1 sets four lines so each is smaller and 'BOOK THEM DIRECT' closes up. X3's two long words fill the line box and the third line drops away. This is a legibility observation from the rendered test, not a preference.
what_is_not_done: No 4K upscale. EP007 upscaled only after the pick; that was a separate 2-credit job.
No owner pick. These are options.
No upload, no thumbnail set in YouTube Studio, no launch/links.json entry.

framing_round_2.prompted_by: owner, 2026-10-09: 'no i dont want the same exact framing for this. let's change it'
framing_round_2.reading: Round 1 reproduced EP007's composition exactly: presenter in the right third, thumb pointing back, three lines of type down the left. The owner is rejecting that layout for this episode, not the standard behind it. What stays: the episode's own cold-open cast and set, the presenter in frame for authenticity, text that speaks to the viewer's aspiration in this episode's terms, and the claim boundaries. What changes: where everyone sits in the frame.
framing_round_2.experiment_design: All four carry the same words, HELP HER KEEP THEM, so framing is the only variable. Choosing a frame and choosing a line are separate decisions and mixing them would make neither readable.

framings.name: Beside her, behind the desk
framings.what: The presenter is inside the scene, standing beside the innkeeper on the staff side of the counter, both over her laptop, he turns to camera. Reads as working alongside her rather than presenting at the viewer.

framings.name: Across the desk, two-shot
framings.what: Camera down the length of the counter. The innkeeper on her side, the presenter on the guest side, the open guest book between them. A consultation, not a piece to camera.

framings.name: Object forward
framings.what: The laptop screen and the reservation fill the foreground with the relay address on it, innkeeper soft behind, presenter small at the right edge. The mechanism is the hook and the people are context.

framings.name: Wide room
framings.what: The inn's front hall wide and quiet, innkeeper small behind her desk, presenter standing nearer camera at left but not dominating. Cinematic rather than a face in the corner.

unchanged: that no pick has been made

readings.F1: Warm and equal, and the only one where both faces are large. But he is standing behind the counter on the staff side, which reads as a second innkeeper or a partner in the business. That is the claim boundary this episode has to hold: the practice helps the inn, it does not run it. A caption cannot undo what the picture says. Flagged, not fatal, but it is the one with a boundary problem.
readings.F2: The relationship is right: he is on the guest side, she is behind the counter, and the open guest book between them is the episode's own mechanism. Reads as a working conversation she is part of rather than a piece to camera. Survives 168px with both people still recognisable.
readings.F3: Strongest text at every size and the relay address is the episode's actual hook. Two costs: the screen is unreadable below about 320px, so the hook only works large; and his face is cropped hard at the right edge, which looks like an accident rather than a choice.
readings.F4: The best photograph of the four and the most unlike anything else in the lane. At 168px she disappears into the background and it becomes a man alone in a room, which loses the 'her' the line depends on.

framing_round_2.shrink_test_reading: At 168px F2 and F3 hold. F1's single line across the top goes thin and both figures shrink. F4 loses the innkeeper entirely. This is read off the rendered test.

recommendation.why: It is the only one that is both legible at 168px and correct about who is who. F3 is the stronger image at full size but its hook dies small and the edge crop reads as a mistake. F1 is the warmest and has the boundary problem. F4 is the best photograph and the weakest thumbnail.

likeness_round_3.prompted_by: owner, 2026-10-09: 'yes is like F1 and F2 but that doesn't look like me looks odd'
likeness_round_3.diagnosis: The framing directions F1 and F2 are accepted; the face was wrong. Both rounds used ref-C as the likeness source, which is a frame grabbed from the r11 cut. That cut is a 1280x720 review proxy, so his head occupies a few hundred soft pixels. At that quality the generator has to reconstruct the face rather than copy it, and it reconstructed a rounder jaw and a heavier beard. Nothing in the prompt could fix that; the reference was the fault.
likeness_round_3.fix: Use the episode's own locked look still, L3-chambray at 2688x1520, as the likeness anchor. A head and shoulders crop of it was made at 1161x1215 and passed first, with the full still for wardrobe and the inn desk for setting. The prompt now names the features that went wrong by name: lean oval face, narrow jaw, sparse cheek stubble, thin clear-framed round glasses, and says not to round the face, thicken the beard or broaden the jaw.
likeness_round_3.what_the_comparison_shows: Set beside the locked look, the F1 and F2 faces are visibly rounder with a fuller beard. G1 and G3 sit much closer: the jaw narrows, the stubble thins on the cheeks, the glasses are the right shape. G3 is the closest of the three.
likeness_round_3.honest_limit: This is consistency with the episode's established look, not with a photograph of him. L3-chambray is itself a generated still that he approved as his look for this episode. If the face still reads wrong to him, the reference itself is what needs revisiting, not the prompt.

framings.G1: F2's composition, across the desk with the guest book between them.
framings.G2: F1's warmth with the boundary fixed: the counter is now clearly between them, so he reads as a visitor rather than a second innkeeper.
framings.G3: New: him near camera on the guest side, her working behind the counter. Largest face of the three.

line_round_4.prompted_by: owner, 2026-10-09: 'more like this as far as staging. "help her keep them" is too similar to the "help.." in the first one. what are alts?'
line_round_4.staging: F1 and F2 confirmed as the staging direction. Their corrected-likeness equivalents are G2 and G1.
line_round_4.problem: HELP HER SELL was EP007's line. Repeating the construction on No. 002 makes the second episode read as a template fill rather than a series. The rule it came from still holds: the line carries the verb of the one-person business and speaks to the viewer's aspiration. Only the construction has to change.

alternates.construction: imperative to the viewer, episode's own object
alternates.why: BUILD is the channel's own verb, from 'build, own, and operate'. The guest book is the thing the episode and Short 03 both turn on, and it is a concrete noun a cold viewer can picture. Three stressed words, sets large.
alternates.boundary: The viewer builds the list; the inn owns it. Correct on both counts.

alternates.why: Shortest of the set, so it sets biggest and survives 168px best. States exactly what the practice does.
alternates.risk: Drops 'her', so the picture has to carry who it is for. In this staging it does.

alternates.why: Warmest of the four and the relationship is exactly right: you hand it over, she keeps it. 'The list' is the episode's plainest word for the mechanism.
alternates.boundary: Good. It is explicitly hers, which is the thing the episode argues.

alternates.construction: contrast, names the adversary without naming it
alternates.why: The sharpest and the most likely to stop a scroll. Carries the whole conflict in four words.
alternates.boundary: Fine, but it is closer to a problem frame than an aspiration, which is the thing the owner corrected on EP007.
alternates.risk: The comma makes it two beats, which sets smaller.

rejected.why: 'Own' reads as the operator owning the data. The episode's argument is the opposite.
Promises an outcome the practice cannot guarantee, and the episode never says to leave the sites.
The episode's own phrase, but abstract to a cold viewer and problem-framed.

line_round_4.test_design: All four rendered on the across-the-desk staging so the line is the only variable. Whichever wins can be set on either staging.
line_round_4.shrink_test_reading: Word count decides it. A2 is two short lines and sets largest, the only one fully legible at 168px. A3 is close behind on four short words. A1's four words pull the type down and 'GUEST BOOK' closes up small. A4 is worst: the comma makes two beats and the longest words in the set, so it sets smallest of the four and is unreadable at 168.

recommendation.why: A2 breaks EP007's construction completely, states what the practice does, and is the only line that survives the sidebar size. It drops 'her', so the picture carries who it is for, and in this staging it does: she is right there behind her own counter. A3 is the pick if keeping the client in the words matters more than the last bit of legibility, and it is the warmer line.

series_formula_round_5.prompted_by: owner, 2026-10-09: 'maybe "help" is a good word for all of the businesses moving forward. that can be the consistent'
series_formula_round_5.status: PROPOSED, not ratified. This is a channel-level standard, not an EP009 decision.
series_formula_round_5.proposal: HELP + pronoun + one verb becomes the recurring thumbnail lockup across the series.
why_it_holds: It states the channel's actual proposition: every episode is a business that helps an owner do a specific thing.

It does the compliance work by default. The EP007 note records 'help' as what kept the promise on the right side of the licensing boundary, the practice prepares and the broker sells. That reasoning generalises.
A recurring shape teaches the viewer where to look. The variable slot becomes 'which business is it this week.'
series_formula_round_5.the_condition: The slot has to be ONE short concrete verb. HELP HER SELL works because SELL is a single hard word. HELP HER KEEP THEM is weaker, not because it repeats HELP but because 'keep them' is two soft words saying something vaguer. The shrink test enforces the same limit independently: at 168px a three-word lockup reads and a four-word one does not.

two_rules_to_settle_if_adopted.rule: The pronoun follows the episode's cast, not the formula.
two_rules_to_settle_if_adopted.why: HELP HER on both No. 001 and No. 002 is accurate, since both owners are women. Carried blindly it becomes a tic implying every small-business owner is a woman. HELP HIM and HELP THEM have to be live options.

two_rules_to_settle_if_adopted.rule: The staging has to carry the variation.
two_rules_to_settle_if_adopted.why: If the words, the type, the palette and the presenter all repeat, consecutive episodes read as one video. The series check shows this is currently handled: No. 001 is a workshop three-shot, No. 002 an inn desk two-shot.

ep009_slot.why: Same three-word metre as HELP HER SELL, and rebook is literally the practice: getting a returning guest to book again, direct.
considered: BOOK DIRECT, four words and the type drops
GO DIRECT, four words and vaguer than rebook

series_formula_round_5.series_check_reading: Set beside No. 001, the formula reads as a series: the same three-line cream lockup, the same weight. The stagings are different enough that they do not read as the same video, which is the risk the formula introduces and the thing that keeps it working.
series_formula_round_5.if_ratified: Write the rule into the packaging standard and the thumbnail memory so later episodes inherit it rather than rediscovering it.

staging_round_6.prompted_by: owner, 2026-10-09: 'help her keep them with me and her behind the desk and the guest across?'
staging_round_6.settles: The line is HELP HER KEEP THEM. The staging is both of them behind the counter with a guest on the near side.
staging_round_6.line_note: With a guest in frame the line gets stronger than it was. 'Keep them' had nothing to point at before; now 'them' is the person walking out of the picture. The earlier objection to it was about repeating EP007's construction, which the owner has since decided is the series constant, so that objection is withdrawn.
staging_round_6.boundary_handled_in_blocking: Putting him behind the counter is the arrangement flagged on F1 as reading like a second innkeeper, and a guest at the desk would normally sharpen that. It is fixed in the blocking rather than by caption: she is the one serving, turned to the guest and talking to him, and he is a step out of the exchange looking at the lens. The picture says she runs the inn and he is the person she brought in.

variants.J1: guest at the left edge from behind, both of them to camera, most balanced
variants.J2: she is handing the key across to the guest, which adds a story beat
variants.J3: him large and near on the right, she is turned to the departing guest, biggest face
